title: [Core] Introduce popleft_n and append_n in FreeKVCacheBlockQueue to further optimize block_pool (#21222)

image.wheel_note: first PyPI release after merge (2025-07-25 > 2025-07-22); picked by gen_tasks.py from PyPI upload dates.

workload.note: Pure Python microbench; imports vllm.v1.core.block_pool.BlockPool + vllm.utils, no CUDA. One run prints both ops.

policy.one_run_is: one `docker run` of the workload cmd per arm per repeat (same image, arm tree swapped in by the prelude)

contention_gate.rules: wait while another tenant uses the GPU (>5 % util or a foreign compute process >1 GiB) or the CPU (load1 > nproc/2)

policy.machine_snapshot: machine.py snapshot per workload run -> data/pr_<n>/work/machine_<arm>_<i>.json

arm_isolation.tree: wipe the wheel's vllm/*.py, copy the arm's vllm/ over site-packages (compiled .so stay)
arm_isolation.files: overlay ONLY task.json:source_files from the arm over the wheel's own tree
arm_isolation.tests_benchmarks: copied from the PR's merge tree to /t without a sibling vllm/ package

policy.noise_model: measure.py: paired log-speedup, MAD sigma, theta = clip(k*sigma, theta_min, theta_max) with k/theta from config.yaml:measure

headline: get_new_blocks

reported.gain_evidence: ### benchmark scripts - Get new blocks improved from 0.15ms to 0.008ms - Free new blocks improved from 33us to 9us
reported.experiments_note: reported = numbers from the PR body (author's machine)

author_hardware_args.text: - Get new blocks improved from 0.15ms to 0.008ms
- Free new blocks improved from 33us to 9us

standalone.run_baseline: docker run --rm --gpus device=0 --shm-size=2g -e CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 -e CUDA_DEVICE_ORDER=PCI_BUS_ID -e HF_HUB_DISABLE_PROGRESS_BARS=1 -v $PWD/data/pr_21222:/task:ro -v $PWD/.weights/hf:/root/.cache/huggingface -e ARM=baseline vllm-task:21222 -lc 'A=/base; site=$(python3 -c "import vllm,os;print(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(vllm.__file__)))"); find "$site/vllm" -name "*.py" -delete; cp -a $A/vllm/. "$site/vllm/"; ln -sfn $A /src; rm -rf /t && mkdir -p /t && cd /gold && for d in tests benchmarks pyproject.toml conftest.py; do [ -e "$d" ] && cp -a "$d" /t/; done; cd /t; python3 benchmarks/kv_cache/benchmark_block_pool.py --num-gpu-blocks 100000 --num-iteration 1000 --allocate-blocks 10 50 100 500 1000'
standalone.run_pr_solution: docker run --rm --gpus device=0 --shm-size=2g -e CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 -e CUDA_DEVICE_ORDER=PCI_BUS_ID -e HF_HUB_DISABLE_PROGRESS_BARS=1 -v $PWD/data/pr_21222:/task:ro -v $PWD/.weights/hf:/root/.cache/huggingface -e ARM=pr_solution vllm-task:21222 -lc 'A=/gold; site=$(python3 -c "import vllm,os;print(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(vllm.__file__)))"); find "$site/vllm" -name "*.py" -delete; cp -a $A/vllm/. "$site/vllm/"; ln -sfn $A /src; rm -rf /t && mkdir -p /t && cd /gold && for d in tests benchmarks pyproject.toml conftest.py; do [ -e "$d" ] && cp -a "$d" /t/; done; cd /t; python3 benchmarks/kv_cache/benchmark_block_pool.py --num-gpu-blocks 100000 --num-iteration 1000 --allocate-blocks 10 50 100 500 1000'
standalone.note: The image already holds both trees (/base = baseline commit, /gold = the PR's merge commit); the one-liner swaps the chosen tree over the installed wheel exactly like run_one.sh's prelude, then runs the workload cmd from /t (the merge tree's tests/ + benchmarks/).
